answer: When an agent economy slashes identities together instead of one at a time, a farm's size turns against it. Keys that join in one comet burst, or share timing and wording traces, are grouped by an auditor into a single knoll. Each key posts a bond; if one key in a knoll cheats, every key in it is slashed, and the fine scales with knoll size, so n clones risk about n² while an honest loner risks one bond. New keys also wait on a probation ledge under random spot audits. The weak point is clones adding noise to look unrelated, which raises their running cost.
